info.text:
The FTC received 1,358,253 identity theft reports in 2025, about one every 23 seconds (our math), up from about 1.14 million in 2024. This guide walks through every step in order: a free credit freeze at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion (free by federal law since Sept 21, 2018), free weekly credit reports at AnnualCreditReport.com, fraud alerts (1 year initial, 7 years extended), locking down your accounts, the IRS Identity Protection PIN, and exactly what to do at IdentityTheft.gov if it happens. Plus the common mistakes and a one-screen checklist.

Sources: FTC Consumer Sentinel Network Data Books (2020-2024; Mar 2025); FTC press release (Mar 2025); FTC testimony to the Joint Economic Committee (Mar 25, 2026); Experian citing FTC 2025 Consumer Sentinel data (2026); FTC consumer guidance on credit freezes and fraud alerts (Sept 2018) and free weekly credit reports (Oct 2023); IRS.gov IP PIN guidance and IRS newsroom; FTC IdentityTheft.gov; Javelin Strategy & Research Identity Fraud Study (Apr 2026).

News and education, not financial advice.
